1.assumed: Microwaves have wavelengths from about 1 mm to tens of cm; a few cm is typical.

2.assumed: Three forces in equilibrium form a closed triangle when drawn tip-to-tail.

3.assumed: Significant diffraction needs the de Broglie wavelength comparable to the atomic spacing.

4.assumed: R = ρL/A, so the gradient of R against L is ρ/A.

5.assumed: sin C = 1/n gives C ≈ 42°; incidence above C gives total internal reflection.

6.assumed: Power = force component along motion × velocity: Fv cos θ.

7.assumed: Series cells add e.m.f. and internal resistance; ε = I(R + r_total).

8.assumed: KEmax depends on frequency not intensity; emission is instant; one photon frees one electron.

9.assumed: Series wires carry the same current; same copper means same carrier density.

10.assumed: Resistance depends on dimensions; resistivity is a material property, unchanged by length.

12.assumed: eV₀ ≈ hc/λ: green has shorter wavelength than red so higher threshold p.d.

13.assumed: Unpolarised light has all planes equally, so a single rotating filter passes constant intensity.

14.assumed: Free fall from rest: v increases linearly with t, gradient g.

15.assumed: Resolve vertically: two tension components T cos θ balance the weight.

16.assumed: Equilibrium means forces on one body balance; third-law pairs act on different bodies.

new: water waves slow in shallower water
17.assumed: Frequency is fixed by the source; waves slow in shallow water.

18.assumed: Filament resistance rises with temperature, taking a bigger share of p.d.

19.assumed: Total current into a junction equals total current out.

20.assumed: Positive charge gain means electrons lost; number = Q/e.

21(a).assumed: k = gradient of force–extension graph, with mm converted to m.

21(b).assumed: Micrometer measures diameter at several places; average; A = πd²/4.

21(c)(i).assumed: E = (F/A)/(x/L) and F = kx combine to give kL/A.

21(c)(ii).assumed: Substitute values; percentage uncertainties add for products and quotients.

21(c)(iii).assumed: A value is consistent if its difference from the accepted value is within the uncertainty.

22(a).assumed: In longitudinal waves particles oscillate parallel to energy transfer, forming compressions and rarefactions.

22(b)(i).assumed: Incident and reflected waves superpose; in phase gives antinodes, antiphase gives nodes.

22(b)(ii).assumed: Amplitude falls with distance and at reflection, so unequal waves can't fully cancel; closer to reflector they match better.

22(b)(iii).assumed: Adjacent nodes are λ/2 apart; v = fλ.

22(b)(iv).assumed: Measuring across several node spacings reduces percentage uncertainty.

23(a).assumed: Work = charge × p.d., using e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

23(b).assumed: One photon gives energy hf to one electron; emission only if hf ≥ work function.

23(c)(i).assumed: Intensity sets photon arrival rate; one photon frees one electron; current = charge per second.

23(c)(ii).assumed: Photon energy hf × emission rate gives power; intensity = power/area.

24(a).assumed: Rebound reverses velocity so Δp uses a sign change; F = Δp/Δt with ms converted.

24(b).assumed: Horizontal velocity is constant, so horizontal distance = speed × time of flight.

25(a).assumed: Human reaction time (~0.2 s) is comparable to the intervals; video gives finer timing.

25(b).assumed: Avoid parallax by viewing the scale at eye level / perpendicular.

25(c).assumed: Constant distance per equal time interval means constant (terminal) speed.

25(d).assumed: Rearrange the given formula for radius, then double for diameter.
